newsitem.title: CANADA: Onex Corp. to buy IBM Canada's Celestica unit.
newsitem.headline: Onex Corp. to buy IBM Canada's Celestica unit.

text.p: Canadian turnaround specialist Onex Corp said on Tuesday it agreed to acquire electronics maker Celestica Inc., a unit of IBM's Canadian subsidiary, in a C$750 million ($550 million) deal.

It is the largest acquisition to date for Toronto-based Onex, an investment company with interests in airline catering and auto parts. Last summer, Onex lost a C$2.3 billion ($1.7 billion) takeover bid for Canadian brewer John Labatt Ltd.
Celestica, which employs about 1,000 people, produces memory products and power systems and also provides contract manufacturing services for Canadian and international customers.
IBM Canada, a unit of IBM Corp., established Celestica as a wholly owned unit in January 1994. IBM said its subsidiary had reached a stage where independent ownership was the next logical step.
Celestica has assets of more than C$600 million ($440 million) and annual revenues of C$3 billion ($2.2 billion).
It operates a one million square-foot manufacturing complex in Toronto and a design facility in Endicott, New York.
Onex said it plans to reposition Celestica as a stand-alone company and boost its non-IBM business. Celestica will continue to be a major supplier to IBM under a multi-year supply agreement.

"It is our intention to substantially grow the non-IBM business while continuing to strengthen the relationship and develop further business with IBM," Onex vice-president Anthony Melman said in a statement.
Onex said it will invest at least C$100 million ($73 million) in equity in Celestica, making it the company's biggest shareholder and giving Onex voting control.
The companies said final agreements are expected in the next 60 days.
